source.name: Cloudflare Radar
source.note: Crawler selection and purpose classification follow Cloudflare Radar, which measures observed crawler traffic rather than estimating importance. Traffic share moves month to month, so no ranking is stored here — only membership and purpose, which are stable.

search.label: Search engines
search.upside: Pages can be discovered and ranked in the major search indexes.
search.downside: Pages cannot be crawled, so they will not appear in these search engines. This is rarely intended outside a staging environment.

ai_search.label: AI answer engines
ai_search.upside: The site can be cited as a source in AI-generated answers, which is an increasingly common way people arrive at a page.
ai_search.downside: The site cannot be cited in AI-generated answers. Unlike training crawlers, these send referral traffic, so blocking them forfeits visits.

ai_user.label: User-triggered AI fetches
ai_user.upside: When someone asks an assistant to open a page on this site, it loads.
ai_user.downside: These requests are made because a person asked an assistant to open the page. Blocking them turns a real visit into an error, and it is usually collateral damage from a rule aimed at training crawlers.

social.label: Social link previews
social.upside: Links shared on social platforms and in chat render with a title, description and image.
social.downside: Links shared on these platforms will render as a bare URL with no title, description or image, which measurably reduces click-through.

ai_training.label: AI training crawlers
ai_training.upside: These crawlers may use the site's content as model training data.
ai_training.downside: These crawlers collect content to train models and send no traffic back. Blocking them is common practice — they are the most disallowed group on the web — and it does not affect search rankings.
